featured_reviews.name: Sajeev Francis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Royal Apartment CHS is an older construction, but it is reasonably maintained and managed. The property has stood the test of time and continues to provide a comfortable living environment for its residents. The management team does a commendable job in ensuring that the building remains in good condition, addressing any issues promptly and efficiently.

Despite its age, the building has a certain charm and character that newer constructions often lack. The common areas are kept clean, and the facilities are functional. The residents seem to have a sense of community, which adds to the overall positive atmosphere of the place.

One of the key strengths of Royal Apartment CHS is its location. Situated in a convenient area, it offers easy access to essential services, shops, and public transportation. This makes it an ideal choice for those who value convenience and accessibility.

While there may be some signs of wear and tear, the management's efforts to maintain the property are evident. Regular maintenance and timely repairs ensure that the building remains safe and habitable. The staff is responsive and attentive to the needs of the residents, which is a significant plus.

Overall, Royal Apartment CHS is a reliable and well-managed place to call home. It may not have the modern amenities of newer buildings, but it makes up for it with its charm, community spirit, and excellent management. If you're looking for a comfortable and well-maintained place to live, Royal Apartment CHS is worth considering.

featured_reviews.name: Ankur Gohil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having met Aku from the SlumGods crew – a hip-hop collective empowering children through teaching them the elements of hip-hop in Dharavi, during the #sassoondockartproject, @guidovanhelten spent sometime in Dharavi, making photographs, and understanding more about the space through the eyes of Aku and his friends who gave him a first hand sense of the vibrant street culture of Dharavi.

The artist decided he wanted to paint two boys, Bboy Pro kid and Bboy Abhishek, framed mid-action doing what they do best … dance!

The mural is a representation of the future of youth culture and the strength of creativity and expression in Dharavi through dance, graffiti and hip hop culture. It is reflective of the emerging and contemporary face of Dharavi.

It is a must visit place for everyone to witness the mural in person

The roads leading to the building are narrow, filled with parked vehicles and people who do not step out of the way. Taxi drivers curse you for making them drop you here. The surrounding shops and structures are unpainted, gloomy and dilapidated. Reaching the railway station means you will have to take the bridge over the slums.

The lift system in the building is also very bad. Despite having three elevators in A-wing, their synchronisation is terrible. Men and women have different timings to access the gym. There is a termite problem in most flats. The only good part of the building are the neighbours, security and caretakers who are very kind.

featured_reviews.name: Mario Menezes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Actually our cousins live here. So we were strolling in the compound the other day and I cannot express in words how disappointed I was on seeing such cheap finishing. I don’t know if it’s just incomplete (they moved almost a year ago. Does it really take that long?) or it’s intended to be that way. So instead of walls, at the backside of the building there are ‘patras’. You know the ones that you find at construction sites and in chawl houses. It spoils the whole show of a “premium” project. And these guys have paid above ₹5 crores to live here. Does the builder not have any sense? I wonder if majority of the flats are even sold. Paying 5 crores and being treated to ‘patras’ while walking along the compound. It gives such a cheap feeling.

Even the parking lot was supposed to have a nice design but it’s just left open with cheap nets. Makes you really wonder if the cost wasn’t recovered by the builder on account of flats being left unsold. There is no green garden area as promised. It’s just mud lying around which looks so bad and children can’t even play there. They’d promised a nice garden with lush greenery and seats but as I mentioned, it’s all barren land.
Rest everything is good. They have security measures in place, a nice lobby, well maintained passages, waste disposal system and everything but the moment you step out of the building and into the compound you’re gonna be disappointed. Also the views on the east side is disappointing. The flats, especially lower floors overlook a massive slum and even the higher floors don’t have a great view because another tall building happens to be right in front of it.
